style: British BBC police-thriller underscore with spoken dialogue, not singing, English accents only. A four-note minor piano figure circles round and round, insistent and unresolved, over racing electronic percussion, ticking hats and dark analogue synth drones, a thin shimmer of high strings, 140 bpm, paranoid, fight-or-flight. Ambulance two-tone siren, rain on the roof, heart-monitor beeps. Shouted NHS crew: a Brummie Birmingham woman, steady then cracking; a broad Black Country man; a clipped South London driver. At the red light the piano breaks off mid-phrase, everything sinks to one low electric hum. A different voice entirely: a smooth plummy Home Counties politician in his fifties, received pronunciation, petulant and spoilt, muffled behind a car window. Then one clean flatline tone, then nothing.
exclude: American accent, sung vocals, melodic singing, choir, rap, autotune, cheerful, comedy, major key, pop chorus, country, gospel, guitar solo, fade out, music under flatline
lyrics:
[Intro: siren, rain, racing electronic pulse, circling minor piano figure]

[Spoken, shouted, Brummie woman paramedic, breathless]
Sixty over thirty! Fucking hurry up, we're gonna lose him!

[Spoken, shouted, Black Country man paramedic]
Sats dropping, he's peri-arrest!

[Spoken, shouted, South London driver, at the traffic]
Two minutes out! Get the fuck out of the way!

[Brakes. Piano stops mid-phrase. Low hum only]

[Spoken, Black Country man, bewildered]
Why have we stopped?!

[Spoken, posh plummy English politician, petulant, muffled through glass]
I said raspberry-shaped hors d'oeuvres!

[Spoken, quiet, Brummie woman, almost a whisper]
Fifty over twen—

[Flatline tone, no music]

[Silence]

[End]
title: PL r4-line-of-duty-circling-piano
